q-34900.name: Question 1
q-34900.problem: Let $R$ be a $8\times 12$ matrix that has $8$ pivot columns. What is the dimension of the null space of $R?$
q-34900.worked_solution:
We know that $\text{dim(Null}(R))$ is the number of non-pivot columns in $R.$ 

Since $R$ has $12$ columns and $8$ of them are pivots, then the number of non-pivot columns in $R$ is 

$$
12-8=4.
$$

Therefore, $\text{dim(Null}(R))=4.$

q-34904.name: Question 2
q-34904.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.$

II. If $B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=2.$

III. If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.$
q-34904.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is true. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.
$$

- Statement II is false. The matrix $B$ has $2$ pivot column and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- Statement III is true. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

q-34906.name: Question 3
q-34906.worked_solution:
To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $4$th column). 

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))=1.
$$

q-35347.name: Question 4
q-35347.worked_solution:
To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(G))$, we reduce $G$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}G & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ -2 & 3 & -6 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ -6 & -15 & -12 & -16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{9}{2} & \frac{11}{4} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $4$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim}(\text{Null}(G))=0.
$$

q-79345.name: Question 5
q-79345.problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Find $\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C)).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
q-79345.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- The matrix $A$ has $1$ pivot column and $2$ non-pivot columns (namely, the $2$nd and $3$rd columns). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $4$th column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C))=2+1+1=4.
$$
